technical-summary: Session record schema restructured v2 (flat) -> v3 (grouped, omit-if-absent): provider-id/model-id/metadata under 'provider', all four timestamps under 'timing', idle/max-lifetime under 'policy' (whole group omitted when unset), turn-count/request-ids under 'activity'; close-reason/error stay top-level but only when actually set. v2->v3 migration added alongside the existing v1->v2 step (both run transparently on read). Added sessions_store.py accessor helpers (session_provider_id, session_model_id, session_turn_count, etc.) and updated every read call site across sessions.py/dispatch.py/api.py; transition_session_record and record_session_turn now write into the grouped locations directly (no shim). Found and fixed a real bug this surfaced: list_execution_sessions sorted by the now-nonexistent top-level r['created-at'], which would have crashed session listing entirely. Also fixed gpt-auto's GptAutoSessionTransport ignoring its own GptAutoConfig.cdp_url in favor of an always-unset duplicate constructor parameter with a hardcoded default -- any configured custom CDP port was silently ignored. Along the way, discovered and fixed a second real, independent gpt-auto resume bug: _resolve_workspace's resume branches called client.evaluate('window.location.href=...') assuming an active browser page already existed, which is false right after a fresh CdpClient connection ('No active page'); replaced with client.new_tab(url), which both guarantees a page and navigates in one step -- verified this closed the failure by driving a real close->resume->recall round trip against a live ChatGPT session via CDP. Registered three production error codes that were raised but never added to error-resolutions.yaml (VAL-AGW-102, VAL-AGW-103, RES-AGW-103), which is itself an architecture-doctrine violation this work surfaced -- any code path hitting them previously crashed with a generic ValueError instead of the intended typed error. Updated ~10 test call sites for the new schema shape and fixed unrelated pre-existing test gaps the investigation surfaced (missing surface_id in several session-binding test fixtures; one test asserting since-removed pre-hardening v1-migration behavior, rewritten to assert the current fail-closed contract). Verified: full unit session test sweep (100% pass), plus two directly relevant Docker E2E suites on real Linux against the real pi-acp bridge -- pi-acp-resume-e2e (drives AcpAgentSessionTransport.open_resumed() through a genuine SIGKILL-and-resume) and pi-rpc-tap-e2e (real multi-turn tool-calling conversation) -- both pass (one transient tool-calling flake on first run, passed clean on retry, consistent with that test's own documented small-model uncertainty).
user-summary-candidate: Restructured how gateway sessions are stored internally (cleaner, grouped shape instead of one flat list of fields) and fixed several bugs it surfaced along the way, including a session-listing crash and a gpt-auto resume bug.

technical-summary: dispatch_request now routes a no-isolation provider's plain one-shot submit (no session_id/session_keep_alive) through the existing ephemeral-session pattern in _dispatch_session_request (open, one turn, auto-close) instead of the disposable-subprocess worker path, which categorically requires full-isolation. full-isolation and partial-isolation routing, worker_host.py's UNS-AGW-076 gate, and SH06's Docker-validated subprocess isolation model are unchanged. UNS-AGW-076's resolution text rewritten to state it no longer applies to no-isolation providers and to point at session_keep_alive as the working alternative. Added a unit test proving the new routing never touches execute_isolated_provider_turn for a no-isolation provider.
user-summary-candidate: agent_task_submit now works for browser/CDP-driven and other no-isolation providers (e.g. gpt-auto) even without opening a live session explicitly -- previously every plain one-shot submit for these providers failed immediately with UNS-AGW-076.

technical-summary: Migrate Claude, Qwen, Antigravity provider MCP config paths from hardcoded ~ to project-local .mcp.json via callable path resolvers. Updated loader.py to resolve dotted refs for both managed_config and mcp_config kinds. Updated tests to use project-local paths instead of home-scoped fixture.
user-summary-candidate: Migrate Claude/Qwen/Antigravity MCP config to project-local .mcp.json

technical-summary: Added new directory constants (CONFIG_DIR_NAME, RUNTIME_DIR_NAME, LINTING_DIR_NAME) to names.py with helper path resolvers. Updated pi.yaml config_path from .mcp.json to .audiagentic/config/mcp.json. Created shared linting config YAMLs for Python, YAML, and TypeScript under .audiagentic/config/linting/.
user-summary-candidate: Centralize project config paths and establish shared linting configuration

technical-summary: Corrected a concurrent in-flight implementation of CC60 (root-config declutter): Pi's mcp.mechanism.config_path was set to ".audiagentic/config/mcp.json", which -- per RV929's read of the actual installed pi-mcp-adapter/config.ts getConfigSources() -- silently breaks MCP discovery for any bare/manual `pi` launch outside AUDiaGentic (root .mcp.json is one of pi-mcp-adapter's own natively-scanned sources). Retargeted to ".pi/mcp.json", a source pi-mcp-adapter already natively scans (pi-project), so no discovery is lost. Also fixed two remaining stale .coding-lsp/ references the .audiagentic/runtime/coding-lsp/ cache migration missed: coding-lsp.yaml's files: entry and test_provider_lsp_e2e.py's assertion.
user-summary-candidate: Fixed Pi's MCP config location so moving it off the project root doesn't break MCP discovery for manual `pi` CLI usage outside AUDiaGentic.

technical-summary: Provider descriptor loading is now resilient to per-provider errors: load_providers_from_directory() wraps each descriptor load in try/except, collecting failures in a module-level _load_errors list (loader.py) instead of raising and crashing the whole gateway. Skipped providers are logged at WARNING with file path and error, plus a summary after load_providers(). A new providers_api.get_provider_load_errors() accessor exposes residual failures, surfaced through gateway_overview()'s new diagnostics block (providers_loaded, skipped_count, errors) and forwarded unchanged by the agent_task_gateway_overview MCP tool. Added test coverage (previously missing) exercising the skip-not-crash path, the error-collector reset, and the diagnostics block's reporting/omission of errors.
user-summary-candidate: One bad provider config file no longer takes down the whole gateway — invalid provider descriptors are now skipped with a warning, and operators can see which providers failed to load via the gateway overview.

technical-summary: Implemented CC58: shared lint config under .audiagentic/config/linting/ now projects to two distinct targets. (1) Native tool config -- ruff.toml, pyrightconfig.json, and .yamllint at project root, written by the new coding_lsp/lint_projection.py module, read directly by ruff/pyright/yamllint and therefore by both the CLI harness and VS Code's own extensions. "line-length" suppression for provider YAML descriptors is a yamllint per-rule ignore glob, not a yaml-language-server setting (verified against the installed yaml-language-server package's settingsHandlers.js -- no such key exists there). (2) .vscode/settings.json's yaml.* keys (validate/completion/schemas/customTags -- the genuinely VS-Code-only part), written through a new providers/surfaces/host_settings.py that reuses extensions_json.py's host-adapter-routed isolation pattern; HostAdapter gained a settings_manifest field (hosts.yaml: vscode.settings-manifest) instead of hardcoding the path. Wired into coding_lsp_bootstrap._on_enabled, idempotent on re-run. Also fixed a stale test (test_load_claude_yaml) asserting Claude's old literal ~/.claude/mcp.json path against the CC55 resolver-based project-local config_path.
user-summary-candidate: Shared lint rules now generate real config files (ruff.toml, pyrightconfig.json, .yamllint, VS Code settings) automatically, so every harness and editor enforces the same rules from one source of truth.

technical-summary: Extended CC58's lint-config projection with TypeScript support (follow-up to the initial Python/YAML implementation). typescript.yaml's compilerOptions projects to tsconfig.json (merged into any existing file so hand-authored include/exclude/references survive re-projection, matching the same merge discipline used for .vscode/settings.json). format.semi/singleQuote/trailingComma project to .prettierrc.json using prettier's real documented option names. format.tabSize/insertSpaces project to a [*.{ts,tsx}] section in .editorconfig via a new section-preserving merge helper, rather than duplicating them into .prettierrc.json's non-standard tabWidth/useTabs or into VS Code settings -- .editorconfig is a genuine cross-editor standard (VS Code, IntelliJ, vim, emacs all read it natively), so all three TypeScript outputs stay in the native-tool-config bucket with no VS Code-only glue required.
user-summary-candidate: TypeScript projects now get the same automatic lint-config generation as Python/YAML -- tsconfig.json, Prettier config, and .editorconfig all stay in sync with one shared source of truth.

technical-summary: Relocate coding-LSP generated state beneath the centralized AUDiaGentic runtime cache path and update the public config API plus dependency, API, and scoped-install tests for the new path contract.
user-summary-candidate: Coding-LSP generated state now lives under the centralized .audiagentic runtime cache instead of a root-level project directory.
